transcription_uncertainties.detail: Selected voice word is retained, not replaced by conjectural Greek vision. English[therewas] states only the minimal nominal existence; the exact relation to throne/appearance/circle is not resolved or invented.
ActualDillmann848 circle/roundness range retained. No adopted Greekτροχός or plural wheels.
All English copular supplies are visibly bracketed and explained; no added seeing/hearing verb or new Geʽez glyph.

translation.text: I looked and saw within it a lofty throne. Its appearance [was] like crystal, and its circle [was] like the shining sun. And [there was] the voice of the cherubim.[a]

footnotes.text: The selected final words are literally “and the voice of the cherubim.” That voice word is retained. The bracketed words supply English copulas for nominal phrases, not an unprinted hearing or seeing verb. The text does not specify how the voice relates to the throne’s appearance, so the English leaves that relation open rather than changing voice into a conjectured vision. Circle can also denote roundness; no different Greek wheel expression is adopted. The low confidence and these grammatical limits are essential to this critical rendering.
